events.opp.mapmaker.title: The Mapmaker's Request
events.opp.mapmaker.body: A mapmaker studies a finished coastal chart in distress. "I used the northern stars for bearings, but no one can check them." An error could send ships astray. The pay is generous.
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.a.label: Measure the bearings again
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.a.outcomes.s: Two places are half a degree off. The corrected map sells at the harbor that winter. Your name appears in tiny letters on the back.
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.a.outcomes.f: Three measurements give three values. The mapmaker pays half and seeks someone else. You are embarrassed, but you did not lie.
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.b.label: Teach the mapmaker to take bearings
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.b.outcomes.s: Skilled hands learn quickly. No more bearing-check jobs arrive, but the mapmaker sends you many other clients.
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.b.outcomes.f: The longer you explain, the stiffer the mapmaker's expression grows. Finally: "Could you just check it for me?"
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.c.label: Say you are busy
events.opp.mapmaker.choices.c.outcomes.o: The map sells unchanged. In spring, rumors tell of a ship leaving its course. You cannot know whether that map caused it.
events.opp.night-caller.title: A Call at Midnight
events.opp.night-caller.body: A knock at midnight. An unfamiliar servant holds a lantern. "My master wants a star reading. Now." A carriage waits. Advance payment rests in the servant's hand.
events.opp.night-caller.choices.a.label: Enter the carriage
events.opp.night-caller.choices.a.outcom: You observe from the mansion roof until dawn. More than the results, your patron likes your admission of what you do not know. You receive another three times the advance.
Clouds never clear. You see nothing. The patron does not reclaim the advance, but never calls again.
events.opp.night-caller.choices.b.label: "Come in daylight and I'll help"
events.opp.night-caller.choices.b.outcom: The servant looks troubled but leaves. Three days later, a formal messenger arrives from the house. The fee is better than the midnight offer.
events.opp.night-caller.choices.c.label: Close the door
events.opp.night-caller.choices.c.outcom: You lie down as the lantern recedes. In the morning, a few coins wait outside. Whether apology or mockery, you cannot tell.
events.opp.night-market-ledger.title: The Night Market Ledger
events.opp.night-market-ledger.body: At dusk, an elderly merchant struggles over a ledger in a market corner. "The numbers won't balance. My eyes aren't what they were..." The merchant stops you and asks for help. Tonight may be long.
events.opp.night-market-ledger.choices.a: Work through the night to balance it
Near dawn, you find the faulty line. Without a word, the merchant gives you a handful of silver and spreads your name around the market.
The numbers never balance. Still, the merchant offers a cold bowl of soup and rice. "Thank you. Young eyes can't always help either."
events.opp.night-market-ledger.choices.b: Bring a friend who is quick with numbers
You are not close enough to Harin yet
Harin lights two candles and sorts the ledger in half an hour. The merchant pays both of you. Harin presses their share into your hand.
events.opp.night-market-ledger.choices.c: The sound of turning ledger pages follows you a long time. Tonight, you have time for the stars.
events.opp.old-instrument.title: Something in the Storeroom
events.opp.old-instrument.body: While cleaning the tower storeroom, you uncover an instrument wrapped in cloth. It appears in no record. The academy says to throw it away. A scrap dealer offers to buy it.
events.opp.old-instrument.choices.a.outc: It is a hundred-year-old navigation protractor, accurate even by modern standards. As you restore and use it, professors come to look one by one.
You take it apart but cannot reassemble it. Six pieces remain. Gu looks at them. "Six left means you took out six wrong in the first place."
events.opp.old-instrument.choices.b.labe: Sell it to the scrap dealer
events.opp.old-instrument.choices.b.outc: The price is surprisingly generous. That troubles you enough to return a few days later. It has already sold.
events.opp.old-instrument.choices.c.outc: You remember its place as you shut the storeroom. You think you will return when your hands improve. Such promises are seldom kept.
events.opp.pawned-book.title: The Pawnshop Book
events.opp.pawned-book.body: An old astronomy volume sits in a pawnshop window. The academy library stamp suggests someone sold it secretly. The price is high. The owner says not to ask where it came from.
events.opp.pawned-book.choices.a.label: Buy it and return it to the archive
events.opp.pawned-book.choices.a.outcome: The librarian holds it in a long silence. "This vanished ten years ago." No one ever learns who took it. Afterward, there is one more key to the archive.
events.opp.pawned-book.choices.b.label: Report it to the academy
events.opp.pawned-book.choices.b.outcome: When the investigation begins, the pawnbroker gives a name. Someone from the academy, in desperate circumstances. The book returns. The person does not.
events.opp.pawned-book.choices.c.label: Pretend you did not see it
events.opp.pawned-book.choices.c.outcome: Something else fills the window the next day. The book has sold. You wonder where it went, then stop wondering.
events.opp.plague-ward.title: The Fevered Alley
events.opp.plague-ward.body: A fever keeps the southern alley indoors. One physician works alone. The academy forbids students from entering. There is a penalty for disobedience, and no one to help in the alley.
events.opp.plague-ward.choices.a.label: Slip in and help
events.opp.plague-ward.choices.a.outcome: For five days, you carry water and distribute clean blankets. As the fever fades, the physician asks your name. You do not answer. The residents find it out themselves.
On the third day, you catch the fever. The physician puts you to bed instead. After a week, you return to your room. The academy never learns.
events.opp.plague-ward.choices.b.label: Contribute food and blankets, then leave
events.opp.plague-ward.choices.b.outcome: The physician accepts without counting. Ten days later, the alley opens. No one knows who donated. You do not tell them.
events.opp.plague-ward.choices.c.label: Obey the restriction
events.opp.plague-ward.choices.c.outcome: Two weeks later, the alley opens. You hear that several homes are empty. For a while, you take a different route.
events.opp.printing-error.title: A Printed Error
events.opp.printing-error.body: This year's observation almanac is out. Every coordinate in the July chart has shifted down one line. Three hundred copies have already gone out. The editor is the academy's most short-tempered person.
events.opp.printing-error.choices.a.outc: The editor fumes for thirty minutes, then spends thirty more making an errata sheet. At last: "Without you, I wouldn't have known until next year."
You are shouted down for questioning the chart. An errata sheet appears only two months later, credited to someone else.
events.opp.printing-error.choices.b.labe: Make corrections and slip them in quietly
events.opp.printing-error.choices.b.outc: You print three hundred sheets overnight and place them in the archive's almanacs. No one learns who did it. Those using July's chart have no trouble.
events.opp.printing-error.choices.c.outc: In July, several people waste their work. Finding the cause takes two weeks. By then, you almost believe you never saw that chart.
events.opp.rain-archive.title: Rain in the Archive
events.opp.rain-archive.body: Water leaks through the basement archive ceiling. Bundles on the lower shelf are getting wet. The librarian is absent. Moving them must happen now, but they are heavy for one person.
events.opp.rain-archive.choices.a.label: Move them all yourself
events.opp.rain-archive.choices.a.outcom: After twenty bundles, your arms shake. The next day, the librarian asks and records your name.
Halfway through, the bundles collapse. The smell of wet paper stays on your hands for a long time.
events.opp.rain-archive.choices.b.label: Go and call for help
events.opp.rain-archive.choices.b.outcom: Three people finish quickly. Credit is shared. That is fine in its own way.
events.opp.rain-archive.choices.c.label: Save only the top shelf and leave
events.opp.rain-archive.choices.c.outcom: You save only the oldest records. The rest go on the disposal list the next day.
events.opp.rival-school.title: An Offer from the Other School
events.opp.rival-school.body: A professor from the southern school visits. "We charge no tuition. Work for us for three years after graduating instead." The terms seem reasonable. Your remaining tuition is a burden.
events.opp.rival-school.choices.a.label: Refuse
events.opp.rival-school.choices.a.outcom: The professor is not offended. "I expected that. Still had to ask." Somehow Sera hears. Days later, she says only, "I heard."
events.opp.rival-school.choices.b.label: Examine the terms carefully
events.opp.rival-school.choices.b.outcom: Three years' wages are half the going rate. Counting it as tuition repayment leaves you worse off. Seeing your calculation, the professor silently folds the papers.
However you study the numbers, you cannot judge the deal. After three days without an answer, the offer quietly disappears.
events.opp.rival-school.choices.c.label: Accept
events.opp.rival-school.choices.c.outcom: Tuition worries vanish. The academy's people begin treating you subtly differently. You cannot quite put the change into words.
events.opp.stage-understudy.title: An Empty Role
events.opp.stage-understudy.body: Someone from the theater rushes in. A role is vacant tonight: twelve lines, two hours to learn them. No one will recognize you.
events.opp.stage-understudy.choices.a.ou: You deliver all twelve lines correctly. Your hands only start shaking after the curtain falls.
You stall at line six. Another actor catches you. The audience probably does not notice. Probably.
events.opp.stage-understudy.choices.b.ou: You raise and lower the curtain three times. A stage is something entirely different from behind.
events.opp.stage-understudy.choices.c.ou: The audience's voices drift through your window all evening. The pages of your book do not turn easily.
events.opp.stray-cat.title: A Guest Under the Eaves
events.opp.stray-cat.body: On a rainy night, a wet cat huddles under the eaves outside your window. Letting it in makes the room smaller. Leaving it there will weigh on you all night.
events.opp.stray-cat.choices.a.label: Dry the cat and let it in
The cat sleeps beneath your desk. It is gone the next morning, but the room feels less cold that night.
events.opp.stray-cat.choices.b.label: Offer food only
The cat empties the bowl and returns to the rain. Closing the window, you briefly wonder whether you did the right thing.
events.opp.stray-cat.choices.c.label: Close the window
Rain continues for a long time. The pages of your book do not turn easily.
events.opp.strike-kitchen.title: The Silent Kitchen
events.opp.strike-kitchen.body: The academy kitchen workers stop working. They have gone unpaid for four months. The academy cites its budget. Students worry about meals. Both sides ask you to take a side.
events.opp.strike-kitchen.choices.a.outc: The money exists, tied to other budget lines. Once revealed, wages arrive in three days. The academy is not grateful. The workers are.
The accounts stay closed. Both sides learn you spoke up. That year, your bowl in the dining hall is always a little fuller.
events.opp.strike-kitchen.choices.b.outc: For six days, students take turns at the pots. The food is dreadful, but no one goes hungry. When the workers return, students applaud.
After two days, no one comes. The pots cool. You wash up alone. Still, someone ate during those two days.
events.opp.strike-kitchen.choices.c.outc: Two weeks later, wages arrive and the kitchen reopens. No one thanks you. No one blames you.
events.opp.tax-clerk.title: The Tax Clerk's Mistake
events.opp.tax-clerk.body: Market stallholders argue over tax notices. The same stalls have been taxed twice. The clerk insists the rules were followed. The merchants cannot do the sums. A pile of papers is pushed before you.
events.opp.tax-clerk.choices.a.label: Recalculate every notice
You find eleven cases of double taxation. The clerk blushes but corrects them. Everywhere in the market that day, someone offers you a discount.
Two calculations give two different answers. Only after the merchants disperse do you find your error. Too late.
events.opp.tax-clerk.choices.b.label: Mediate between clerk and merchants
Both sides yield a little. The clerk promises a review; the merchants agree to wait three days. Three days later, the notices really are corrected.
The longer you talk, the more each side sees you as the other's ally. Everyone leaves dissatisfied.
events.opp.tax-clerk.choices.c.label: Stay out of it
Days later, several stalls stand empty. The twice-taxed merchants have closed. The market grows that much quieter.
events.opp.wager-table.title: A First-Snow Forecast
events.opp.wager-table.body: The square's merchants ask for a first-snow forecast as they prepare their winter market. Weather is not unrelated to the stars. You have studied that connection. An accurate forecast earns a fee.
events.opp.wager-table.choices.a.label: Make a forecast from your observations
events.opp.wager-table.choices.a.outcome: Your forecast is within two days. The prepared merchants pay you 200 gold and ask for your observations again next winter.
Snow comes nine days later than predicted. You earn no fee, but spend three more days finding the calculation's fault.
events.opp.wager-table.choices.b.label: Help the merchants prepare for winter
events.opp.wager-table.choices.b.outcome: For two hours, you check supply lists with Harin. Moving the goods most vulnerable to cold indoors frees up space. Weather knowledge has its uses in trade.
events.opp.wager-table.choices.c.label: Move on to your next task
events.opp.wager-table.choices.c.outcome: Cold air meets you as you leave the square. The first snow falls three weeks later.
events.path.declaration.title: The Day to Choose a Path
events.path.declaration.body: Sera offers a form. "Time to decide." It asks how you will spend the remaining half-year. Once written, changing it has a cost.
events.path.declaration.choices.star.out: You write Path of Stars. Folding the form, Sera says only, "I thought so." That night, you gain another key to the observation tower.
You write Path of Letters. A place in the inner scriptorium is assigned to you. It is quiet, and a little cold.
events.path.declaration.choices.craft.ou: You write Path of Craft. Without looking at the paper, Gu tosses you the courtyard key.
events.path.declaration.choices.stage.ou: You write Path of the Stage. There is an unnamed role waiting in the next performance.
events.path.declaration.choices.market.o: You write Path of Trade. Harin hands you an entire ledger. "Yours now."
events.path.declaration.choices.people.o: You write Path of People. Moran closes her fan. "You chose a difficult one."
events.path.declaration.choices.none.lab: Write that you have not decided
events.path.declaration.choices.none.out: You submit a blank. Sera accepts it without a word. The remaining half-year is entirely yours to choose.
events.world.bell.title: The Evening Bell
events.world.bell.body: The academy bell rings six times. The day is over. The day still has something left.
events.world.bell.choices.a.label: Watch for a moment
events.world.bell.choices.a.outcomes.onl: You stand until the ringing ends. Six strokes last longer than expected. For that time, you think of nothing.
events.world.blackout.title: Lights Out
events.world.blackout.body: For a royal procession, the whole city extinguishes its lights for three days. The academy is no exception. Three nights without a single artificial light: a chance that comes once in ten years.
events.world.blackout.choices.a.label: Observe for all three nights
events.world.blackout.choices.a.outcomes: Faint stars hidden on ordinary nights emerge in numbers. Three nights make the year's thickest academy record.
You fall asleep the second night. On the third, cold stiffens your hands beyond writing. Still, the first night's page survives and is cited many times later.
events.world.blackout.choices.b.label: Observe the first night and rest afterward
events.world.blackout.choices.b.outcomes: One night is enough. You note twelve faint stars and spend the next two days organizing the notes. The ordered record is more useful than the raw observations.
events.world.blackout.choices.c.label: Help put out the lights
events.world.blackout.choices.c.outcomes: You go from alley to alley extinguishing lamps. When the city is fully dark, you stand in the square and look up. You make no observations, but you witness that moment.
events.world.blackout.choices.d.label: Sleep through all three nights
events.world.blackout.choices.d.outcomes: You sleep through the once-in-ten-years nights. People call it a waste whenever it comes up. After those three days, your body does feel lighter.
events.world.censorship.title: The Banned Book List
events.world.censorship.body: A new royal list bans eleven archive books. Three are used in current lessons. The librarian stands before the shelves for a long time, list in hand.
events.world.censorship.choices.a.label: Copy them before removal
events.world.censorship.choices.a.outcom: Over three nights, you copy the essential passages. The unsigned copies go to the third floor. Years later, someone comes looking for them.
On the second day, the librarian finds you. Your copies are seized; you receive a warning. Later, the librarian quietly says, "I wanted to as well. But I have a position to keep."
events.world.censorship.choices.b.label: Challenge the list
events.world.censorship.choices.b.outcom: You submit evidence that the three classroom texts are scholarly works. Two are removed from the list. The third never returns.
The objection is not accepted. Somewhere, the fact that you objected is recorded. The record follows you for years.
events.world.censorship.choices.c.label: Remove the books as ordered
events.world.censorship.choices.c.outcom: You pack eleven books and carry them to the basement. Before closing the box, you read every title. Later, you find and read four elsewhere.
events.world.comet.title: An Unannounced Arrival
events.world.comet.body: At three in the morning, something new hangs in the northeastern sky. No almanac mentions it. The tower fills with people opening their notebooks. The question is who will publish accurate coordinates first.
events.world.comet.choices.a.label: Find the coordinates first
events.world.comet.choices.a.outcomes.su: In two hours, three points give you an orbit. It is within half a degree of the royal corps' later figures. Everyone in the tower that night sees it.
events.world.comet.choices.a.outcomes.fa: Clouds and impatience shake your measurements. By morning, two points turn out to be the same position. Someone else's values go on the board.
events.world.comet.choices.b.label: Simply watch for a long time
events.world.comet.choices.b.outcomes.on: You watch for two hours without opening your notebook. Nearby people call out numbers as if from far away. That night's sky color stays with you.
events.world.comet.choices.c.label: Give up your place and descend
events.world.comet.choices.c.outcomes.on: Too many people crowd the telescope. You bump into those climbing up. It is visible from your room's window too.
events.world.eclipse.title: The Sun That Set at Noon
events.world.eclipse.body: The predicted total eclipse arrives. The whole city fills the square. The academy sets out its instruments. For roughly three minutes, everyone chooses what to see.
events.world.eclipse.choices.a.label: Record the corona
You draw twelve pages in three minutes. Your hand moves before thought catches up. Those twelve pages enter that year's almanac supplement.
The three minutes end during your second page. Two unfinished sheets remain, with the sorrow of perhaps never seeing it again.
events.world.eclipse.choices.b.label: Explain it to the crowd
You explain to about twenty people at one edge of the square. A child asks why stars appear at noon. As you answer, the crowd doubles.
Your words may be too difficult; people drift away. When the eclipse actually begins, you are the one person not looking up.
events.world.eclipse.choices.c.label: Just watch
You watch all three minutes without recording or explaining. You even see the birds fall silent in the darkened day. That appears in no record.
events.world.first-frost.title: The First Frost
events.world.first-frost.body: At dawn, white frost coats the windowsill. Your fingertips tell you the season has moved one step.
events.world.first-frost.choices.a.label: Watch for a moment
events.world.first-frost.choices.a.outco: You touch it briefly. Cold travels from fingertips to wrist, then fades. You think it is time to prepare for winter.
events.world.first-snow.title: The First Snow
events.world.first-snow.body: The window shows white. In this city, everyone traditionally stops work and goes outside for the first snow. Even the academy bell stays silent.
events.world.first-snow.choices.a.label: Go outside
events.world.first-snow.choices.a.outcom: Everyone from the academy is in the square: professors and gatekeepers alike. No one goes inside until the snow stops.
events.world.first-snow.choices.b.label: Watch from the window
events.world.first-snow.choices.b.outcom: You open the window from your room. The square's sounds are distant. Your hands cradle the ink to keep it from freezing. That night's writing is longer than usual.
events.world.first-snow.choices.c.label: Continue your work
events.world.first-snow.choices.c.outcom: You ignore the custom and stay at your desk. You progress, but cannot quite focus. By the time you go out that evening, the snow has melted.
events.world.flood.title: The Overflowing River
events.world.flood.body: Three days of rain overflow the river. The southern village floods, driving people into the square. The academy opens its hall, but food and blankets run short.
events.world.flood.choices.a.label: Spend three days helping in the hall
events.world.flood.choices.a.outcomes.on: You carry meals and mind children. On the third night, an elder asks for constellation stories. The whole hall falls quiet. For the first time, you understand what teaching means.
events.world.flood.choices.b.label: Measure the river and issue a forecast
events.world.flood.choices.b.outcomes.su: Comparing three days of levels and rainfall, you predict the water will fall in two days. It is exactly right. People trust the forecast and pack their things.
events.world.flood.choices.b.outcomes.fa: The predicted day comes without relief. Packed belongings are unpacked. You cannot bring yourself to visit the hall for three days.
events.world.flood.choices.c.label: Donate what money you have
events.world.flood.choices.c.outcomes.on: The dean puts out a collection box. You donate without writing a name. That day's money buys twenty blankets.
events.world.flood.choices.d.label: Attend lessons
events.world.flood.choices.d.outcomes.on: Four people sit in class. The professor follows the schedule. Beyond the window, you can see the hall.
events.world.foreign-scholar.title: A Scholar from Far Away
events.world.foreign-scholar.body: A scholar arrives from the east. The constellations have wholly different names; the calculations differ too. The results are nearly the same. Half the academy is intrigued. Half is uneasy.
events.world.foreign-scholar.choices.a.o: The methods diverge at exactly three points. At all three, the eastern method is more accurate. Your comparison enters next year's textbooks.
Aligning the terms takes two weeks. The comparison never begins. Before leaving, the scholar gives you a chart.
events.world.foreign-scholar.choices.b.o: For a month, you follow like a shadow. On departure, the scholar leaves a correspondence address. Your letters continue for two years.
Your words keep crossing, causing more hindrance than help. Eventually gestures work better. That is not so bad either.
events.world.foreign-scholar.choices.c.o: After two months, the scholar leaves. Years later, a book bearing that name enters the archive. You study its cover for a long time.
events.world.guild-dispute.title: The Guild's Complaint
events.world.guild-dispute.body: The diviners' guild complains to the academy. Students offer free star readings, leaving members unable to earn a living. It is true. You are among those students.
events.world.guild-dispute.choices.a.lab: Meet the guild and agree on fees
events.world.guild-dispute.choices.a.out: Student fees are set at half the guild rate. In return, the guild teaches an academy class. Both sides gain something.
Negotiations break after three hours. The guild asks the dean to ban student readings. The dean agrees. One source of pocket money is gone.
events.world.guild-dispute.choices.b.out: Six come to learn. Two are twice your age. Teaching someone who has come to learn is easier than expected.
events.world.guild-dispute.choices.c.out: Your income falls, but your mind is at ease. Months later, the guild leader offers you a meal. You share a cup of tea.
events.world.harvest-fair.title: The Harvest Fair
events.world.harvest-fair.body: For three days, stalls cover the square. Academy students can have a space too. Sell if you have something. Otherwise, simply look around.
events.world.harvest-fair.choices.a.outc: Everything sells in two days. On the third, you only take orders. You return with five times your starting capital.
The next stall is cheaper and prettier. You close before selling half. The leftover pictures go on your room's wall. That has its merits too.
events.world.harvest-fair.choices.b.labe: Help the stallholders all three days
events.world.harvest-fair.choices.b.outc: You carry goods and help with sums. Pay is modest, but merchants learn your name. Afterward, you visit the market without needing to ask prices.
events.world.harvest-fair.choices.c.outc: You circle the square three times in three days. You buy and sell nothing, yet return in a good mood.
events.world.lantern-night.title: The Lantern Festival
events.world.lantern-night.body: Lanterns hang over the square. Simply walking among the crowd makes your heart a little brighter.
events.world.lantern-night.choices.a.out: You make two circuits beneath the lanterns. Familiar faces greet you. Some call you by name.
events.world.new-chancellor.title: A New Dean
events.world.new-chancellor.body: The dean changes. At the first assembly, the new dean says, "This school has looked only at the sky for too long. It must prove its usefulness." The professors' expressions divide.
events.world.new-chancellor.choices.a.ou: You publish a condensed booklet of navigational star charts. The dean mentions it at assembly. The harbor guild orders one hundred copies.
The project passes, but no one uses it. The attempt to prove usefulness proves none.
events.world.new-chancellor.choices.b.la: Write in defense of basic research
events.world.new-chancellor.choices.b.ou: Your noticeboard essay grows to five pages in three days as others add their own. The dean is said to stand before the wall for a long time.
The essay is removed after one day. You never learn by whom, and have nowhere to ask.
events.world.new-chancellor.choices.c.la: Take no interest in the change
events.world.new-chancellor.choices.c.ou: The numbers on your observation chart do not change with the dean. Your records accumulate at the same pace as before.
events.world.plague-edict.title: The Month of Closed Gates
events.world.plague-edict.body: An epidemic in a neighboring city closes the gates for a month. Supplies stop, prices rise, and visiting lecturers cannot enter. Several gaps appear in the timetable.
events.world.plague-edict.choices.a.labe: Fill the empty lessons with self-study
events.world.plague-edict.choices.a.outc: You study alone in a classroom without a lecturer. Learning that no one assigned leaves a different mark. When the gates open a month later, the lecturer is surprised.
events.world.plague-edict.choices.b.outc: You buy oil and candles in advance. By the third week, prices triple. After using what you need, you share the rest. The sharing is remembered longer.
You buy flour, but the gates open earlier than expected. Prices fall instead. The flour spoils.
events.world.plague-edict.choices.c.outc: The month simply passes. Conserving candles cuts your night study. You gain the habit of rising early instead.
events.world.royal-visit.title: The Royal Inspection
events.world.royal-visit.body: Royal visitors will inspect the academy. Someone must explain the observation tower. The professors pass the task around. The dean decides to choose an apprentice.
events.world.royal-visit.choices.a.label: Volunteer
events.world.royal-visit.choices.a.outco: You guide them for thirty minutes using ordinary words. The chamberlain takes out a notebook. That year's royal grant gains an observation budget line.
As your explanation runs long, the visitors grow bored. One final question comes. You cannot answer. The dean says nothing. That lasts longer.
events.world.royal-visit.choices.b.label: Prepare the tower instead
events.world.royal-visit.choices.b.outco: You spend two days cleaning lenses and organizing records. The royal party never sees you. The telescope gives its clearest view of the year.
events.world.royal-visit.choices.c.label: Stay back
events.world.royal-visit.choices.c.outco: Another apprentice guides the visit without trouble. You spend the day in the library. Nothing happens.
events.world.tower-crack.title: A Crack in the Tower
events.world.tower-crack.body: A crack runs through the tower's north wall. The mason says it will not collapse immediately. The academy says it has no budget. Use is forbidden meanwhile. No one knows how long observations must stop.
events.world.tower-crack.choices.a.label: Raise money for repairs
events.world.tower-crack.choices.a.outco: Two months of visiting merchants, guilds, and graduates raise enough. After repairs, a donor plaque goes by the entrance. Your name is at the bottom.
You raise less than half. Still, it pays for temporary supports. Half the tower reopens.
events.world.tower-crack.choices.b.label: Build a temporary observation deck
events.world.tower-crack.choices.b.outco: You build a wooden platform on the hall roof. Lower and with a narrower view, but usable. It remains even after the tower is repaired.
The first wind tilts it. No one is hurt, but the academy orders it removed. Taking the wood, Gu says, "Didn't check the foundations."
events.world.tower-crack.choices.c.label: Wait for the tower to reopen
events.world.tower-crack.choices.c.outco: It takes four months. You read a normal year's worth in that time. When you first climb back and use the eyepiece, your hands tremble.
