events.cond.burnout.enter.title: The Morning Your Hands Stopped
events.cond.burnout.enter.body: You wake but cannot get up. Daylight fills the window. Everything you must do today runs through your mind, yet you cannot bring yourself to move a finger. Your mentor knocks, then leaves.
events.cond.burnout.enter.choices.a.labe: Spend two days under the covers
events.cond.burnout.enter.choices.a.outc: Two days later, you open the window and let the breeze in. You tell yourself that two days are all you have lost.
events.cond.burnout.enter.choices.b.outc: The next morning, warm porridge and a short note wait outside your door. "Rest is part of training." The handwriting is larger and rounder than usual.
events.cond.burnout.enter.choices.c.labe: Pay for warm meals and rest
events.cond.burnout.enter.choices.c.outc: Warm meals and a day of rest ease your mind. After lying down all day, your body feels a little sluggish.
events.cond.burnout.exit.title: A Morning Two Days Later
events.cond.burnout.exit.body: You wake after losing two whole days. Outside, daylight carries on as though nothing happened. The backlog still covers your desk. Strangely, it no longer frightens you.
events.cond.burnout.exit.choices.a.label: Choose just one unfinished task
events.cond.burnout.exit.choices.a.outco: You start with the smallest task. Once it is done, the next looks smaller. You finish three that day and leave the rest for tomorrow.
events.cond.burnout.exit.choices.b.label: Rest for one more day
events.cond.burnout.exit.choices.b.outco: You leave another day empty. This time, you choose to do nothing. That makes it different from two days ago.
events.cond.burnout.exit.choices.c.label: Finish the entire backlog today
events.cond.burnout.exit.choices.c.outco: You finish after midnight. You remember finishing, but not what you did. Only you fail to notice that this night is just like the night two days before.
events.cond.disgrace.enter.title: Turned Backs
events.cond.disgrace.enter.body: You greet someone in the square. They pretend not to see you. So do the second and third people. No one tells you what rumor is spreading. Even telling you would mean taking a side.
events.cond.disgrace.enter.choices.a.lab: Find out what people are saying
events.cond.disgrace.enter.choices.a.out: The story came from one person, and it was false. Proving that takes two weeks. What you lose during those weeks does not return.
Each question makes the rumor grow. The fact that you are asking becomes another story.
events.cond.disgrace.enter.choices.b.out: You spend four months without responding. The rumor fades on its own. Your work from those months lasts longer than the gossip.
events.cond.disgrace.enter.choices.c.out: You apologize without knowing what you did wrong. Some accept it; others pull farther away. You still do not know which was better.
events.cond.disgrace.exit.title: The First Greeting
events.cond.disgrace.exit.body: Someone in the square greets you first. It has been so long that you are slow to answer. "I heard the wrong story about that business." A few months unravel in a single sentence.
events.cond.disgrace.exit.choices.a.outc: They tell someone else, who tells another person. The correction follows the same path as the rumor.
events.cond.disgrace.exit.choices.b.outc: They look uncomfortable but tell you everything. Knowing it makes it seem trivial. Losing months to something so small feels unfair. Still, it is better to know before letting it go.
events.cond.failed.enter.title: A Second Failure
events.cond.failed.enter.body: The review results are on the noticeboard. This is the second time. The rules say an apprentice who fails twice cannot enter the advanced course. Reading that takes ten seconds. Understanding takes longer.
events.cond.failed.enter.choices.a.label: Keep attending for the remaining months
events.cond.failed.enter.choices.a.outco: The advanced course is closed, but lessons are still open. Freed from worrying about reviews, you follow your interests. A few pages from that year become the best work of your life.
events.cond.failed.enter.choices.b.label: Read the rules again from the beginning
events.cond.failed.enter.choices.b.outco: The sixteenth clause contains an exception. Two supervising professors can sign a request for a new review. No one has ever used it. There is not even a form.
Three readings reveal no loophole. The rule is short and plain. Even confirming that helps settle something inside you.
events.cond.failed.enter.choices.c.label: Go to Sera
events.cond.failed.enter.choices.c.locke: Requires at least 35 affinity with Sera
events.cond.failed.enter.choices.c.outco: Sera offers no comfort. Instead, she hands you next month's observation schedule. "These aren't assessed. The slots are empty because no one will take them." You eventually fill every slot.
events.cond.injury.enter.title: A Misstep at Night
events.cond.injury.enter.body: You miss a step on the observation tower stairs. Nothing is broken, but your wrist swells. The physician orders three weeks without using it. Three weeks means six turns.
events.cond.injury.enter.choices.a.label: Follow the physician's advice
events.cond.injury.enter.choices.a.outco: You study things that need no handwork. You read three times your usual amount. By the time your hand heals, your mind is full.
events.cond.injury.enter.choices.b.label: Pay for a faster recovery
events.cond.injury.enter.choices.b.outco: A skilled bonesetter restores your wrist in three days. It is expensive, but it feels like buying back lost time.
events.cond.injury.enter.choices.c.label: Keep working through the pain
events.cond.injury.enter.choices.c.outco: Your wrist takes twice as long to heal. The notes you make while injured are so shaky that you must copy them all again.
events.cond.injury.exit.title: The Day the Bandage Comes Off
events.cond.injury.exit.body: You unwrap your wrist. Its strength has not fully returned, but it works. Old Gu takes your hand and bends each finger. "That's better. Go gently at first."
events.cond.injury.exit.choices.a.label: Start again with something light
events.cond.injury.exit.choices.a.outcom: You polish a small lens. The first is ruined; by the second, your hand remembers. Old Gu watches in silence.
events.cond.injury.exit.choices.b.label: Return straight to your usual work
events.cond.injury.exit.choices.b.outcom: Two days later, your wrist aches again. Old Gu clicks his tongue, then wraps a fresh bandage. "I said gently."
events.cond.slump.enter.title: The Same Line Again
events.cond.slump.enter.body: You are reading the same sentence for the fourth time. Its meaning will not sink in. Yesterday was the same, and so was the day before. Closing the book feels like falling behind. Leaving it open teaches you nothing.
events.cond.slump.enter.choices.a.label: Take three full days off
events.cond.slump.enter.choices.a.outcom: On the third day, the pages begin to turn on their own. You cannot say what has changed.
events.cond.slump.enter.choices.b.label: Visit the hot spring
events.cond.slump.enter.choices.b.outcom: Only when the hot water reaches your shoulders do you realize how tense they were.
events.cond.slump.enter.choices.c.label: Sit at your desk anyway
events.cond.slump.enter.choices.c.outcom: Two hours pass. You manage half a page. You are left with that half page and a slightly heavier heart.
events.cond.slump.exit.sera.title: The One Who Changes the Candle
events.cond.slump.exit.sera.body: Sera enters without a word and replaces your spent candle. She sits across the desk. "You don't have to do anything today. I'll be here too."
events.cond.slump.exit.sera.choices.a.ou: Neither of you speaks for two hours. When half the candle is gone, Sera gets up. Only after the door closes do you open your book. This time, you can read.
events.cond.slump.exit.sera.choices.b.ou: "When I was twenty-five, I spent half a year like this. If someone had sat beside me, it might have been three months." Sera says no more.
events.cond.slump.exit.spring.title: The Northern Hot Spring
events.cond.slump.exit.spring.body: A fellow apprentice draws you a map. "There's a hot spring half a day's walk away. No one around, just hot water." Going costs money and two days of lessons. Sitting here for two days would gain you nothing anyway.
You sink into the water up to your neck and look at the sky. It has been a long time since you saw stars without counting constellations. Your shoulders feel lighter on the way home.
You sit beside the spring without entering. Half a day of walking clears your thoughts. You spend no money.
The map goes into a drawer. You think you might go someday. That thought alone makes the night a little easier.
events.cond.slump_light.enter.title: Dulled Fingertips
events.cond.slump_light.enter.body: You get the same calculation wrong three times. What worked yesterday will not work today. You are not ill and have not forgotten what you know. Something between your hands and mind has slipped out of place.
Practice less and return to basics
You revisit your first-year lessons. On the third day, you find the fault: a chart you memorized incorrectly long ago.
You press on with the error. Later, you must redo the whole section. Yet remembering that you did not stop eventually helps.
Explaining it aloud shows you where you are stuck. Your listener barely says anything, yet receives your thanks.
You start speaking, then swallow the words. They are busy, and you cannot quite name the problem. Still, that night is a little better.
events.cond.slump_light.exit.title: A Returning Touch
events.cond.slump_light.exit.body: When you pick up your pen, your hand moves first. What failed yesterday works today. You do not know what changed. You leave it alone, afraid that examining it will make it vanish.
events.cond.slump_light.exit.choices.a.o: You clear the entire blocked section in a day. Your wrist aches that evening, but it is a satisfying ache.
events.cond.slump_light.exit.choices.b.l: Do your usual amount and stop
events.cond.slump_light.exit.choices.b.o: You finish your normal amount and close the book. Your hand works the next day, and the day after. Perhaps not overdoing it is why.
events.fin.awaken.title: What Opened
events.fin.awaken.body: The final observation. As you look through the eyepiece, the things that drifted apart for twelve months fall into place. Calculation and instinct give the same answer. You know nights like this are rare.
events.fin.awaken.choices.a.label: Write it down
events.fin.awaken.choices.a.outcomes.onl: You write eleven pages before dawn. Later, they go into a locked shelf on the archive's third floor: the section for observations still awaiting verification.
events.fin.awaken.choices.b.label: Tell no one
events.fin.awaken.choices.b.outcomes.onl: You step back from the eyepiece and cover the telescope. You alone keep what you saw that night. No one ever tells you it was wrong.
events.fin.bond.title: Faces on the Last Night
events.fin.bond.body: Someone waits in the courtyard on the night before graduation. It is the face you have seen most often these twelve months. "Tomorrow it's over." They say it, but make no move to leave. The courtyard lamps go out one by one.
events.fin.bond.choices.a.label: Tell the story of all twelve months
The story continues after every lamp goes dark. At dawn, the gatekeeper passes and pretends not to notice. Half of what you say is forgotten by morning; the other half stays for years.
events.fin.bond.choices.b.label: "It's the next beginning"
They repeat the words twice, then nod. At graduation the next day, you do not look for each other. You have already said what mattered.
events.fin.failed.title: A Name Returned
events.fin.failed.body: Your name has been crossed off the graduation roll. A clause says anyone who fails two reviews cannot graduate. No one mentioned it beforehand. The gatekeeper carries your bags. "That's all for this year, then."
events.fin.failed.choices.a.label: "I'll come back next year"
events.fin.failed.choices.a.outcomes.onl: The gatekeeper leaves the roll open. "A crossed-out place stays empty for a year. It's a rule." It is not a rule, but you do not ask.
events.fin.failed.choices.b.label: Leave without a word
events.fin.failed.choices.b.outcomes.onl: From the hill outside the gate, you look back once. Another light already shines in the room at the far end of the third floor.
events.fin.quiet.title: Packing in the Afternoon
events.fin.quiet.body: The last room on the third floor. You have a little more luggage than when you arrived. The constellations on the windowsill remain, joined by one you carved only halfway. It belongs to the next occupant now.
events.fin.quiet.choices.a.label: Leave the unfinished carving
events.fin.quiet.choices.a.outcomes.only: You look back before closing the door. Two unfinished constellations sit side by side: one by a stranger, one by you.
events.fin.quiet.choices.b.label: Leave a note
events.fin.quiet.choices.b.outcomes.only: You stick a note inside the drawer. "The 3rd floor is cold in winter. Stuff paper into the window gaps." You write exactly what the previous occupant wrote.
events.fin.quiet.choices.c.label: Take your bags and leave
events.fin.quiet.choices.c.outcomes.only: Descending the stairs takes thirty seconds. Those same stairs seemed much longer when you first arrived.
events.fin.renown.title: The Order of Names
events.fin.renown.body: The graduation order is posted. Your name is near the top. The academy calls names by reputation, not grades. The student beside you checks twice. "Is that really you?"
events.fin.renown.choices.a.label: Take your place at the front
events.fin.renown.choices.a.outcomes.onl: When your name is called, applause starts at the back. The people you met over twelve months are there. Stepping off the platform, you look their way once.
events.fin.renown.choices.b.label: Ask to be called later
events.fin.renown.choices.b.outcomes.onl: The organizer looks troubled, then changes the order. The last name receives the longest applause. You did not plan that.
events.fin.undeclared.title: The Empty Career Field
events.fin.undeclared.body: The career field on your graduation papers is blank. Sera waits with her pen. "Leave it blank and you're simply a graduate. That's fine too." The last snow melts outside. "Still, decide what to call these twelve months before you leave."
events.fin.undeclared.choices.a.label: "Leave it as graduate"
events.fin.undeclared.choices.a.outcomes: Sera puts down the pen. "A blank is an answer too." Only your name and dates remain. You think that is accurate.
events.fin.undeclared.choices.b.label: "Write that I spent twelve months learning"
events.fin.undeclared.choices.b.outcomes: Sera writes exactly that. Yours is the second document in academy history with a sentence in the career field instead of a title. She never tells you whose was first.
events.milestone.s1.title: The First Seasonal Review
events.milestone.s1.body: A nameboard hangs in the academy courtyard. It is the first seasonal review: a chance to see what three months have built. The backs of those in front seem unusually straight.
events.milestone.s1.choices.a.label: Step forward as prepared
events.milestone.s1.choices.a.outcomes.s: You pass the quarter 1 review. Your name moves to the middle row. There is no fanfare, but a few people brush your shoulder as they pass.
events.milestone.s1.choices.a.outcomes.f: Your name stays on the bottom row after the quarter 1 review. You stare at the board for a long time, then turn away.
events.milestone.s1.choices.b.label: Step aside and prepare for next time
events.milestone.s1.choices.b.outcomes.o: You do not enter the quarter 1 review. No one says anything. That stays with you longer.
events.milestone.s1.watched.title: A First Review in the Spotlight
events.milestone.s1.watched.body: It is your first review, but the courtyard is busier than usual. Word has spread that a well-known apprentice is appearing. It takes a moment to realize the name they mean is yours.
events.milestone.s1.watched.choices.a.ou: You pass the quarter 1 review. The onlookers nod as if they expected it. Their calm feels heavier than applause.
You fail the quarter 1 review. With so many witnesses, word travels fast. The silence around it the next day is harder to bear.
events.milestone.s1.watched.choices.b.la: Ignore expectations and work as usual
events.milestone.s1.watched.choices.b.ou: You pass the quarter 1 review. Your unremarkable composure becomes the story instead.
You fail the quarter 1 review. Your usual effort was not enough. At least that much is clear, making your next step easier.
events.milestone.s1.watched.choices.c.la: Step aside and prepare for next time
events.milestone.s1.watched.choices.c.ou: You decline to enter in front of the gathered crowd. The murmuring follows you for a long time.
events.milestone.s2.title: The Midsummer Review
events.milestone.s2.body: The second review. You know better than anyone what was missing last time. Heat from the courtyard warms the back of your neck.
events.milestone.s2.choices.a.label: Step forward as prepared
events.milestone.s2.choices.a.outcomes.s: You pass the quarter 2 review. Your name moves to the middle row. There is no fanfare, but a few people brush your shoulder as they pass.
events.milestone.s2.choices.a.outcomes.f: Your name stays on the bottom row after the quarter 2 review. You stare at the board for a long time, then turn away.
events.milestone.s2.choices.b.label: Step aside and prepare for next time
events.milestone.s2.choices.b.outcomes.o: You do not enter the quarter 2 review. No one says anything. That stays with you longer.
events.milestone.s2.cornered.title: A Summer with No Retreat
events.milestone.s2.cornered.body: The second review. One more failure closes the advanced course to you. Everyone who has read the rules knows this. No one mentions it in the courtyard.
events.milestone.s2.cornered.choices.a.l: Pass this time, whatever it takes
events.milestone.s2.cornered.choices.a.o: You pass the quarter 2 review. Only after seeing your name on the board do you breathe. You stand there for a long time.
You fail for the second time. The rules take their course. You do not cry before the noticeboard, or in your room that night.
events.milestone.s2.cornered.choices.b.o: You pass the quarter 2 review with a low score. A pass is a pass. An examiner says as they go by, "Surviving takes skill too."
Even playing safe is not enough. Your second failure is final. You never know whether playing safe caused it.
events.milestone.s2.cornered.choices.c.o: You decide the result by staying outside. Only later do you learn that withdrawing counts as a failure.
events.milestone.s3.title: The Frosted Review
events.milestone.s3.body: The third review. People say you can already see what everyone will become. Your hands feel cold before the board.
events.milestone.s3.choices.a.label: Step forward as prepared
events.milestone.s3.choices.a.outcomes.s: You pass the quarter 3 review. Your name moves to the middle row. There is no fanfare, but a few people brush your shoulder as they pass.
events.milestone.s3.choices.a.outcomes.f: Your name stays on the bottom row after the quarter 3 review. You stare at the board for a long time, then turn away.
events.milestone.s3.choices.b.label: Step aside and prepare for next time
events.milestone.s3.choices.b.outcomes.o: You do not enter the quarter 3 review. No one says anything. That stays with you longer.
events.milestone.s3.favorite.title: The Favorite in the Frost
events.milestone.s3.favorite.body: The third review. A predicted ranking is pinned beside the noticeboard. You do not know who put it there, but your name is first. There are always people who do this.
events.milestone.s3.favorite.choices.a.o: You pass the quarter 3 review. Whoever posted the ranking was right today. Unfamiliar apprentices greet you as you leave.
You fail the quarter 3 review. The ranking vanishes the next day. You never learn who took it down.
events.milestone.s3.favorite.choices.b.o: You pass the quarter 3 review. Without the sheet, the courtyard is quiet. In that quiet, you do as well as you normally do.
You fail the quarter 3 review. Later, you are glad you took down the ranking.
events.milestone.s3.favorite.choices.c.o: You stay outside while your name is still at the top. The sheet remains until evening.
events.milestone.s4.title: The Final Review
events.milestone.s4.body: The final review. A whole year gathers here. Nothing remains behind you. Ahead is one door.
events.milestone.s4.choices.a.label: Step forward as prepared
events.milestone.s4.choices.a.outcomes.s: You pass the quarter 4 review. Your name moves to the middle row. There is no fanfare, but a few people brush your shoulder as they pass.
events.milestone.s4.choices.a.outcomes.f: Your name stays on the bottom row after the quarter 4 review. You stare at the board for a long time, then turn away.
events.milestone.s4.choices.b.label: Step aside and prepare for next time
events.milestone.s4.choices.b.outcomes.o: You do not enter the quarter 4 review. No one says anything. That stays with you longer.
events.milestone.s4.barred.title: Outside the Courtyard
events.milestone.s4.barred.body: The final review day. Failed apprentices may not enter. You lean against the outer wall and listen as names are called one by one.
events.milestone.s4.barred.choices.a.out: You hear every name. Several belong to people you know, including some you taught. You clap from outside the wall.
events.milestone.s4.barred.choices.b.out: You climb until the review sounds fade. You look through the eyepiece in daylight. Nothing is visible, but your hands move with familiar ease.
events.milestone.s4.barred.choices.c.out: You return to your room before the review ends. Packing takes less time than expected. You spend the remaining time looking at the windowsill constellations.
events.npc.gu.01.title: The Broken Chisel
events.npc.gu.01.body: Old Gu holds a broken chisel. He says he has used it for thirty years. "Even iron grows old." He looks at you and asks whether to forge it anew or bury it.
events.npc.gu.01.choices.a.label: Offer to forge it yourself
events.npc.gu.01.choices.a.outcomes.succ: Half a day at the forge leaves the chisel shorter, but sharp. Gu places it in your hand.
events.npc.gu.01.choices.a.outcomes.fail: The metal spits three times. Gu takes the tongs. "That's enough for today." He does not seem angry.
events.npc.gu.01.choices.b.label: Suggest burying it
events.npc.gu.01.choices.b.outcomes.only: You bury it beneath the persimmon tree behind the workshop. Gu pats the earth twice and stands. "You choose the next one."
events.npc.gu.01.choices.c.label: Buy him a new one
events.npc.gu.01.choices.c.outcomes.only: Gu studies the new chisel for a long time, then puts it in a drawer. He keeps using the broken one.
events.npc.gu.02.title: Sweeping the Filings
events.npc.gu.02.body: The workshop is open. Old Gu faces away, grinding a lens. Three days of metal filings cover the floor. He must hear you, but does not turn. A broom rests in the corner.
events.npc.gu.02.choices.a.label: Pick up the broom in silence
events.npc.gu.02.choices.a.outcomes.only: An hour later, the floor is visible. Gu has not turned once. As you leave, a cup of cold tea waits beside the door.
events.npc.gu.02.choices.b.label: "Can I help with anything?"
events.npc.gu.02.choices.b.outcomes.only: "The ones who ask don't help." Gu keeps his eyes on the lens. When you remain standing there, he eventually adds, "Broom's over there."
events.npc.gu.02.choices.c.label: Watch him grind the lens
events.npc.gu.02.choices.c.outcomes.only: You watch for two hours. The same motion repeats about three hundred times. On the three hundred and first, you finally see the difference. Gu speaks at last. "Now you've seen it."
events.npc.gu.03.title: What the Hands Know
events.npc.gu.03.body: Old Gu ruins three lenses in a row. He studies his open hands, then pushes the work toward you. "My eyes are gone. Only the hands remain." An unfinished eyepiece lies on the bench.
events.npc.gu.03.choices.a.label: "Let me be your eyes"
events.npc.gu.03.choices.a.outcomes.succ: You watch while Gu cuts. The fourth lens survives. He holds it to the light, then silently puts it in a drawer. There are no other lenses like it inside.
events.npc.gu.03.choices.a.outcomes.fail: You point to the wrong place. The fifth lens breaks too. Gu sweeps up the glass without anger. "It was like this when my sight went. Not knowing you're wrong is the frightening part."
events.npc.gu.03.choices.b.label: "You should see a physician"
events.npc.gu.03.choices.b.outcomes.only: Gu keeps refusing until you say you have already paid. He says nothing on returning, but halves his working hours from that day.
events.npc.gu.03.choices.c.label: "I'll finish the eyepiece"
events.npc.gu.03.choices.c.outcomes.only: It takes three days. Gu inspects the finished eyepiece and taps two flaws with a fingernail. "Here and here. The rest is good." It is the highest praise he can offer.
events.npc.gu.03.choices.d.label: "Let's stop for today"
events.npc.gu.03.choices.d.outcomes.only: Gu removes his apron without protest. That is stranger still. As you leave the darkened workshop, he says, "Tomorrow my eyes may be worse, or better. That part isn't mine to choose."
events.npc.gu.04.title: The Last Telescope
events.npc.gu.04.body: Behind a cloth at the back of the workshop stands a frame two stories tall. Gu began this telescope thirty years ago and stopped twenty years ago. His scorched hands spread the plans. "Eleven parts missing. Plans are here. I can't do it alone."
events.npc.gu.04.choices.a.label: "Let's make all eleven together"
events.npc.gu.04.choices.a.outcomes.succ: The final part fits on a snowy dawn. You take turns at the eyepiece. After thirty years, the telescope sees the sky for the first time. Gu takes a long time to yield his turn.
events.npc.gu.04.choices.a.outcomes.fail: You make nine parts, then stall at the tenth. That section of the plans has worn away. Gu covers the frame again. "Nine is better than twenty years."
events.npc.gu.04.choices.b.label: "What if we ask others?"
events.npc.gu.04.choices.b.outcomes.only: Five people you invite fill the workshop. Gu dislikes it at first, but says nothing when all eleven parts are ready in two weeks. He insists on doing the assembly himself.
events.npc.gu.04.choices.c.label: "I can't take this on"
events.npc.gu.04.choices.c.outcomes.only: Gu folds the plans and replaces the cloth. "That's that, then." The cloth at the back is never lifted again.
events.npc.gu.05.title: The Workshop Sign
events.npc.gu.05.body: Old Gu takes the sign off the workshop door. Thirty years of weather have almost erased its letters. "Needs carving again. Hands won't follow." He pushes a chisel toward you. "Your name or mine. You choose."
events.npc.gu.05.choices.a.label: Carve his name again
events.npc.gu.05.choices.a.outcomes.only: You follow the original letters. Gu hangs the sign and looks up at it for a long time. "Better than mine." Then he adds, "So put your name on the next one."
events.npc.gu.05.choices.b.label: Carve both names side by side
events.npc.gu.05.choices.b.outcomes.succ: Getting the spacing right takes another day. After hanging the sign, Gu pats your shoulder for the first time. His hand is heavy.
events.npc.gu.05.choices.b.outcomes.fail: The chisel slips on the second name. Getting new wood would take days. Gu rubs the scar with a fingertip. "Hang it as it is. A flaw is a record too."
events.npc.gu.05.choices.c.label: "That isn't for me to decide"
events.npc.gu.05.choices.c.outcomes.only: Gu takes back the chisel and hangs the faded sign. "Then faded it stays." Years later, people give the workshop different names after reading it.
events.npc.gu.yun.title: An Old Instrument
events.npc.gu.yun.body: Yun takes an old protractor from their pack and sets it in the workshop. Gu's hands stop. "I made this. Forty years ago." Yun says, "It was my father's."
events.npc.gu.yun.choices.a.label: Sit them down and listen
events.npc.gu.yun.choices.a.outcomes.onl: Their stories last all night. Forty years ago, one made the instrument and the other used it. That night, you hear everything that happened between.
events.npc.gu.yun.choices.b.label: Repair the protractor together
events.npc.gu.yun.choices.b.outcomes.suc: The three of you revive the forty-year-old instrument. Yun uses it to check their plateau measurements again. The values are right. Gu says nothing.
events.npc.gu.yun.choices.b.outcomes.fai: The corroded scale breaks at a touch. Sweeping up the pieces, Gu says, "Forty years is enough." Yun puts the fragments in their pack.
events.npc.gu.yun.choices.c.label: Leave them alone together
events.npc.gu.yun.choices.c.outcomes.onl: You close the workshop door behind you. Their voices continue late into the night. You never ask what they discussed.
events.npc.harin.01.title: Soup for Two
events.npc.harin.01.body: Harin waits beside two bowls of soup and rice. "My treat today." Behind the glasses, Harin's eyes are redder than usual. There are rumors of a serious bookkeeping mistake.
events.npc.harin.01.choices.a.label: Eat without asking
events.npc.harin.01.choices.a.outcomes.o: You empty the bowls in silence as the soup cools. On the way out, Harin says just one thing. "Thanks."
events.npc.harin.01.choices.b.label: Offer to examine the ledger together
events.npc.harin.01.choices.b.outcomes.s: After three hours, you find the faulty entry. Harin removes the glasses and presses tired eyes for a long time. "How did I miss that?"
events.npc.harin.01.choices.b.outcomes.f: Even together, you cannot find the answer. Harin says it was still better than looking alone.
events.npc.harin.01.choices.c.label: Say you have an appointment and leave
events.npc.harin.01.choices.c.outcomes.o: Harin pays for both bowls. The next day, Harin greets you with the usual smile.
events.npc.harin.02.title: The Sound of Abacus Beads
events.npc.harin.02.body: Harin stays after class, working an abacus over a ledger instead of a textbook. Meeting your eyes, Harin adjusts the glasses. "My family runs a soup shop. If I don't balance this tonight, we can't buy supplies tomorrow."
events.npc.harin.02.choices.a.label: "Shall we balance it together?"
events.npc.harin.02.choices.a.outcomes.o: Working together turns an hour into twenty minutes. Harin closes the ledger. "Tomorrow's soup is yours. No charge."
events.npc.harin.02.choices.b.label: "Teach me to keep a ledger"
events.npc.harin.02.choices.b.outcomes.s: Harin has a gift for teaching. Within two hours, you can separate income and expenses. "Learn this and you'll never go hungry."
events.npc.harin.02.choices.b.outcomes.f: The numbers keep slipping away. Harin explains three times without impatience. "Everyone starts like this. My father told me ten times."
events.npc.harin.02.choices.c.label: Say, "See you later," and leave
events.npc.harin.02.choices.c.outcomes.o: Even as the door closes, you hear the abacus. The next day, Harin has dark circles beneath the eyes but says nothing.
events.npc.harin.03.title: A Line Missing from the Ledger
events.npc.harin.03.body: Harin tears out a ledger page. The income column has been empty for three months. "My father left debts. I'm only managing the interest." An attempted smile fails. "Maybe I'll pay this month's tuition and leave."
events.npc.harin.03.choices.a.label: "I can contribute something"
events.npc.harin.03.choices.a.outcomes.o: Harin refuses three times and accepts on the fourth. In return, you receive a written one-tenth share in the soup shop. "Putting it in the ledger is my way."
events.npc.harin.03.choices.b.label: "Let's find a way to repay it"
events.npc.harin.03.choices.b.outcomes.s: You spend three nights recalculating the interest. The creditor checks twice, then changes the terms. That day, Harin cries in front of you for the first time.
events.npc.harin.03.choices.b.outcomes.f: However you turn the numbers, they return to the same place. Harin folds the abacus first. "Looking with me was enough. Alone, I keep seeing it wrong."
events.npc.harin.03.choices.c.label: "Leaving is an option too"
events.npc.harin.03.choices.c.outcomes.o: After a long pause, Harin shakes their head. "Hearing you say that makes leaving feel like a waste." That month's tuition comes from selling one of the shop's soup pots.
events.npc.harin.04.title: A Shop That Sells Stars
events.npc.harin.04.body: Harin unfolds a plan: a shop selling observation tools and constellation pictures beside the soup shop. "No law says we can't sell what we learn." Eyes shine behind the glasses. "Be my partner. You bring the stars; I'll bring the sums."
events.npc.harin.04.choices.a.label: "Yes. But I handle all the stars"
events.npc.harin.04.choices.a.outcomes.s: The first month's sales reach half the soup shop's. By the third month, they surpass it. Half the customers are academy apprentices; the rest are seeing stars for the first time.
events.npc.harin.04.choices.a.outcomes.f: The location is poor. After two months, you close with half your capital left. Harin shuts the ledger. "Failed businesses go in the books too. Next time, we start from here."
events.npc.harin.04.choices.b.label: "My studies come first"
events.npc.harin.04.choices.b.outcomes.o: Harin shows no disappointment. "I thought you'd say that. That's why I asked." The plans go into a drawer, folded but not discarded.
events.npc.harin.04.choices.c.label: "You can use my name"
events.npc.harin.04.choices.c.outcomes.o: Your name appears in small letters on the sign. It doubles the first month's customers. Harin faithfully sends you one-third of the profit. You never visit the shop.
events.npc.harin.05.title: The Last Bowl of Soup
events.npc.harin.05.body: One night near graduation, Harin brings two bowls. "I'm handing over the shop tomorrow. Someone wants to buy it." Across the steam, Harin removes the glasses. You have never seen that face without them. "What do I do now?"
events.npc.harin.05.choices.a.label: "Let's go together. Anywhere"
events.npc.harin.05.choices.a.outcomes.o: Harin puts the glasses back on and smiles. "That's what I ordered two bowls to hear." Until the soup cools, you take turns naming cities you could visit.
events.npc.harin.05.choices.b.label: "People who can count are needed everywhere"
events.npc.harin.05.choices.b.outcomes.s: That night, Harin thinks of three openings. Next month brings an application for the royal procurement office's clerk exam. By the acceptance letter's arrival, a different sign hangs over the old soup shop.
events.npc.harin.05.choices.b.outcomes.f: "I know that." Harin stirs the soup. "Knowing and deciding are different." You decide nothing that night and simply empty the bowls.
events.npc.harin.moran.title: Between Two People
events.npc.harin.moran.body: Moran's trading house plans to buy the whole alley containing Harin's soup shop. Moran asks you to persuade Harin. The price is generous. Harin was born in that alley.
events.npc.harin.moran.choices.a.label: Stand with Harin
events.npc.harin.moran.choices.a.outcome: You tell Moran you cannot do it. She folds her fan, waits, then says, "I thought so." The alley remains unsold. That winter, you pay your own tuition.
events.npc.harin.moran.choices.b.label: Negotiate a better deal
events.npc.harin.moran.choices.b.outcome: You arrange a purchase that keeps the soup shop in place rent-free. Both sides think they have won. Both really have.
Going between them angers both sides. The alley is sold, and the soup shop moves two alleys away. Harin does not blame you. That lasts longer.
events.npc.harin.moran.choices.c.label: Stay out of it
events.npc.harin.moran.choices.c.outcome: You say it is between them and withdraw. The alley sells six months later. Neither ever mentions it to you again.
events.npc.mentor.sera.01.title: A Note Folded Twice
events.npc.mentor.sera.01.body: Sera has left a note on your desk. Inside the twice-folded paper is one line: "Learn nothing today, then come see me." You cannot tell what it means.
events.npc.mentor.sera.01.choices.a.outc: Sera pours two cups of tea and asks nothing. After an hour, you leave with lighter shoulders.
events.npc.mentor.sera.01.choices.b.labe: Bring a summary of today's lessons
events.npc.mentor.sera.01.choices.b.outc: Sera reads to the end and says, "I told you to rest." Still, the three corrections she marks are precise.
events.npc.mentor.sera.01.choices.c.outc: The note is gone the next day. Sera never brings it up again.
events.npc.mentor.sera.02.title: Wrong for Ten Years
events.npc.mentor.sera.02.body: Sera puts an old observation notebook on the desk. The open page is wrong from beginning to end. "Mine. Written at twenty-three. Discovered the error at thirty-three." She looks at you without turning the page. "I taught it wrong for ten years."
events.npc.mentor.sera.02.choices.a.outc: After three hours, you point to the eleventh line. Sera is silent for a long time. Closing the notebook, she says, "It took me three days."
You work all night without finding it. Sera replaces the candle without looking disappointed. "Not finding the error is normal. That's why it took ten years."
events.npc.mentor.sera.02.choices.b.outc: "Because lately you've been afraid of being wrong." Sera puts the notebook in a drawer without locking it. "It stays there. Open it when you're afraid."
events.npc.mentor.sera.02.choices.c.labe: Close the notebook and return it silently
events.npc.mentor.sera.02.choices.c.outc: Sera takes it and briefly studies your face. The lesson ends fifteen minutes earlier than usual.
events.npc.mentor.sera.03.title: The Locked Shelf
events.npc.mentor.sera.03.body: A locked shelf stands on the observation tower's third floor. You have never seen Sera take out its key before. "These observations are unverified. That doesn't mean wrong. It means no one has looked again yet." Dust turns slowly in the candlelight.
events.npc.mentor.sera.03.choices.a.outc: You choose an apprentice's winter observations from forty years ago. Correcting one coordinate makes the rest fit. Sera reads the long-forgotten name aloud.
You work for two weeks, but the original errors are too large. Replacing it, Sera says, "Not being able to verify it is a record too. The next person starts here."
events.npc.mentor.sera.03.choices.b.outc: Sera points to the second shelf from the bottom. Twelve volumes stand together. "What I couldn't finish. I put them here hoping someone would open them someday." Then she places the key in your hand.
events.npc.mentor.sera.03.choices.c.labe: "I think it's too soon for me"
events.npc.mentor.sera.03.choices.c.outc: Sera nods and locks the shelf. "Knowing when to say it's too soon is a skill too." As you descend, you hear her check the lock once more.
events.npc.mentor.sera.04.title: The Unfinished Paper
events.npc.mentor.sera.04.body: Sera offers a manuscript, half dense handwriting and half blank pages. "Submitted three times. Rejected three times. I haven't the strength for a fourth." Snow begins outside. "Submit it under your name. Put mine in a footnote, or don't."
events.npc.mentor.sera.04.choices.a.labe: "I'll submit it under both our names"
events.npc.mentor.sera.04.choices.a.outc: Filling the blank half takes a season. The reply names both authors together. Sera reads it again and again, then hands it back. "You keep it."
The fourth submission is rejected too. This time, the objection is its length, not its argument. Sera laughs as you have never seen before. "Progress."
events.npc.mentor.sera.04.choices.b.labe: "I won't accept it under my name alone"
events.npc.mentor.sera.04.choices.b.outc: Sera puts the manuscript back in her drawer, but does not lock it. "Stubborn." After that, you open the drawer together once a week.
events.npc.mentor.sera.04.choices.c.outc: It is published under your name alone. Scholarship gains a new name. Sera appears in no footnote. She says she does not mind, and seems not to. That stays with you longer.
events.npc.mentor.sera.05.title: The Night the Charts Change Hands
events.npc.mentor.sera.05.body: Sera sets thirty years of observation charts on the desk. The leather cover is dark with use. "This is my last year teaching. I've told the dean." Her voice is unchanged. "Continue it or burn it. It's yours."
events.npc.mentor.sera.05.choices.a.outc: The first page carries Sera's handwriting from age twenty-three. Your hand first appears after her final page. The scripts are so different that the continuity is plain.
events.npc.mentor.sera.05.choices.b.outc: Later, you cannot remember what you said or how. That winter, Sera's resignation returns from the dean's desk. Two hands begin alternating across the charts.
Sera listens to the end, then shakes her head. "Thank you. But I've thought about this a long time." The charts stay with you. Sera leaves the academy in spring.
events.npc.mentor.sera.slump.title: Even Mentors Get Stuck
events.npc.mentor.sera.slump.body: The same calculation has lain on Sera's desk for four days. No progress. She does not hide it, but pushes the paper toward you. "Look. It happens to me too."
events.npc.mentor.sera.slump.choices.a.o: What blocked her for four days falls in half a day with two of you. Sera seems more surprised by that fact than by the answer.
Even together, you cannot solve it. Sera folds the paper. "Two people failing is different from one failing. The problem itself is wrong."
events.npc.mentor.sera.slump.choices.b.o: Sera smiles briefly and clears the desk. There is no lesson that day. You walk twice around the courtyard. The next day, Sera solves the calculation.
events.npc.moran.01.title: A Single Invitation
events.npc.moran.01.body: Moran sends an invitation. There is an empty place at dinner. Formal manners are required, and mistakes will be remembered for a long time.
events.npc.moran.01.choices.a.label: Dress formally and attend
events.npc.moran.01.choices.a.outcomes.s: You speak three times in two hours, each time correctly. On the way out, Moran says, "I'll invite you again."
events.npc.moran.01.choices.a.outcomes.f: You raise your glass in the wrong order. No one points it out. That makes the moment feel longer.
events.npc.moran.01.choices.b.label: Attend in your usual clothes
events.npc.moran.01.choices.b.outcomes.s: Someone comments on your clothes, but your easy laugh relaxes the gathering. Moran says nothing.
events.npc.moran.01.choices.b.outcomes.f: You fidget with your collar all evening. You remember none of the conversation.
events.npc.moran.01.choices.c.label: Decline politely
events.npc.moran.01.choices.c.outcomes.o: You send a short reply. Moran does not answer. Another invitation never comes.
events.npc.moran.02.title: A Favor with a Price
events.npc.moran.02.body: Moran folds her fan and slides over a receipt. This month's tuition is already paid. "Don't be surprised. I invest early in promise." Her fan opens again. "Of course, I'll collect later."
events.npc.moran.02.choices.a.label: "What price?"
events.npc.moran.02.choices.a.outcomes.o: For the first time, Moran closes her fan completely. "It's been a while since anyone asked." She never names the price, but from that day she calls you by name.
events.npc.moran.02.choices.b.label: Bow and accept
events.npc.moran.02.choices.b.outcomes.o: "Clever child." Moran seems pleased. Your purse stays full that month. Two more social invitations arrive instead.
events.npc.moran.02.choices.c.label: "I pay my own tuition"
events.npc.moran.02.choices.c.outcomes.o: Moran retrieves the receipt and smiles. "That stubbornness will appreciate." She never repeats the offer in the following months. Instead, she begins watching where you spend your money.
events.npc.moran.03.title: The Seat Behind the Fan
events.npc.moran.03.body: At a trading-house banquet, Moran seats you beside her. Opposite sit the dean and a royal procurement officer. "You need do nothing. Just sit." Her fan hides half her face. "But watch who interrupts whom."
events.npc.moran.03.choices.a.label: Watch quietly until the end
events.npc.moran.03.choices.a.outcomes.o: You say nothing for three hours. In the carriage, Moran asks, "How many interruptions?" "The officer interrupted the dean four times." Moran taps her knee once with her fan.
events.npc.moran.03.choices.b.label: Speak to the officer first
events.npc.moran.03.choices.b.outcomes.s: Your mention of observations makes the officer lean forward. By evening's end, your name is in the officer's notebook. Moran remains silent behind her fan.
events.npc.moran.03.choices.b.outcomes.f: The table falls silent as you begin. The officer smiles politely and changes the subject. Later, Moran says only, "There is an order to things."
events.npc.moran.03.choices.c.label: Say you feel unwell and leave early
events.npc.moran.03.choices.c.outcomes.o: Moran does not stop you. At later banquets, your seat is no longer beside hers.
events.npc.moran.04.title: What Is Being Bought?
events.npc.moran.04.body: Portraits of sponsored apprentices cover Moran's study wall. Of the twenty-odd faces, most names are unfamiliar. "All failures." Her fan sweeps the wall. "Yet I kept investing every year. Why do you think that is?"
events.npc.moran.04.choices.a.label: "One success pays for the rest"
events.npc.moran.04.choices.a.outcomes.o: Moran shakes her head. "A merchant's answer. Not wrong." She points to an empty frame. "That's yours. I'll hang it whether you succeed or not."
events.npc.moran.04.choices.b.label: "The ones who failed still have lives somewhere"
events.npc.moran.04.choices.b.outcomes.s: Moran does not open her fan for a long time. "Perhaps I've invested for twenty years to hear that." For the first time, you are served tea in her study. No price is mentioned.
events.npc.moran.04.choices.b.outcomes.f: "A kind thing to say." Moran opens her fan and changes the subject. The portraits never come up again.
events.npc.moran.04.choices.c.label: "I won't fail"
events.npc.moran.04.choices.c.outcomes.o: Moran laughs aloud, a sound new to this room. "Twenty-five said exactly that." Yet her fan stays closed. That is what she does when she believes.
events.npc.moran.05.title: The Day No Price Is Collected
events.npc.moran.05.body: Moran burns the sponsorship agreement bearing your name. "I said I'd collect. Now I won't." Ash rises from the brazier. "One condition: someday, do the same for someone. Mention the price. Don't collect it."
events.npc.moran.05.choices.a.label: "I will"
events.npc.moran.05.choices.a.outcomes.o: Moran closes her fan and gives it to you. Inside the handle are twenty-six tiny names. The final space is empty.
events.npc.moran.05.choices.b.label: "Let me pay you back"
events.npc.moran.05.choices.b.outcomes.o: Moran puts the money in a drawer without counting. "One more apprentice next year, then." She adds, "You're the first. To repay me."
events.npc.moran.yun.title: The One Who Cannot Be Sponsored
events.npc.moran.yun.body: After reading Yun's observation records, Moran offers sponsorship. Yun refuses. "I do this so my name won't be written anywhere." Moran looks at you over her fan. "Try persuading them. Such a waste of talent."
events.npc.moran.yun.choices.a.label: Honor Yun's wishes
Moran closes her fan and waits. "That's an answer too." Afterward, she buys Yun's records for the archive without demanding anything in return. No name is written.
events.npc.moran.yun.choices.b.label: Suggest anonymous sponsorship
You arrange funding without a name on the records. Moran gains what she wants; Yun keeps what matters. No such contract exists, so you write a new form.
Both say it cannot exist. Moran says sponsorship without a price is no sponsorship. Yun says any price leaves a name behind. Both are right.
events.npc.rival.eden.01.title: A Way of Remembering Names
events.npc.rival.eden.01.body: At the noticeboard, Eden points to your name beside theirs on this week's observation roster. "So it's you." Eden reads it aloud twice, like someone marking a name rather than learning it.
events.npc.rival.eden.01.choices.a.label: "I've learned your name too"
events.npc.rival.eden.01.choices.a.outco: Eden hesitates, then smiles. "Good, then." Neither of you speaks during that week's observations. Each of you counts how often the other writes.
events.npc.rival.eden.01.choices.b.label: "Let's work well together"
events.npc.rival.eden.01.choices.b.outco: "I won't need any favors." Despite the words, Eden quietly adjusts the telescope angle before leaving the first night. You only notice the next morning.
events.npc.rival.eden.01.choices.c.label: Check the roster again and leave
events.npc.rival.eden.01.choices.c.outco: Eden says something behind you, but you miss it. For the rest of the week, Eden never greets you first in the tower.
events.npc.rival.eden.02.title: Another Sleepless Observer
events.npc.rival.eden.02.body: You meet Eden on the tower landing. They hold the very observation chart that has occupied you for three days. "I thought you'd see it first." Neither smiling nor sneering, Eden offers it.
events.npc.rival.eden.02.choices.a.label: Say, "Let's look together," and sit down
events.npc.rival.eden.02.choices.a.outco: You read the same chart twice before dawn. When you identify the same error in different places, Eden laughs aloud for the first time.
events.npc.rival.eden.02.choices.b.label: "If you saw it first, solve it first"
events.npc.rival.eden.02.choices.b.outco: Eden hands over the chart without protest. The next morning, your name tops the observation record. Eden says nothing all day.
You try to snatch the chart and drop it. Eden waits, arms folded, while you gather the pages. That hurts more. From that day, you watch each other closely.
events.npc.rival.eden.02.choices.c.label: Descend the stairs without a word
events.npc.rival.eden.02.choices.c.outco: Pages turn behind you. Tonight, the tower belongs to Eden.
events.npc.rival.eden.03.title: Each Other's Weaknesses
events.npc.rival.eden.03.body: After joint practice, there is only cold tea. Eden sets down a cup. "I'm not the only one who knows you miss digits in calculations." A pause. "My hands shake. I can't make fine adjustments. No one knows that."
events.npc.rival.eden.03.choices.a.label: "Then let's check for each other"
events.npc.rival.eden.03.choices.a.outco: From that day, a line of the other's handwriting appears on each of your sheets. The professors never discover why both apprentices' accuracy improves together.
events.npc.rival.eden.03.choices.b.label: "Why tell me?"
events.npc.rival.eden.03.choices.b.outco: After a long silence, Eden says, "I can tell someone I want to beat. Because I haven't lost to you." It feels less like boasting than a confession.
"I'm regretting it already." Eden stands with the cup. At the next practice, their hands shake more than usual. You pretend not to see.
events.npc.rival.eden.03.choices.c.label: "We each handle our own weaknesses"
events.npc.rival.eden.03.choices.c.outco: Eden drains the cup and nods. "Right. I was being strange." Eden never shows you their hands again.
events.npc.rival.eden.04.title: One Place
events.npc.rival.eden.04.body: The royal observation corps will accept one apprentice. Only two people at the academy qualify. Eden waits by the notice. "They say if we both apply, both might fail. An examiner told me."
events.npc.rival.eden.04.choices.a.label: "Let's both apply anyway"
events.npc.rival.eden.04.choices.a.outco: Both apply. Both are accepted. The corps creates two unplanned places. The report notes that the applications cite each other's work.
Both apply. Both fail. On the way home, Eden says, "No regrets." You feel the same. For the first time, you walk side by side.
events.npc.rival.eden.04.choices.b.label: "You apply. I won't"
events.npc.rival.eden.04.choices.b.outco: For the first time, Eden is angry. "I wasn't waiting for you to give it to me." Eden never applies. The place goes to another academy. Neither of you gains anything.
events.npc.rival.eden.04.choices.c.label: "I'm applying. You decide for yourself"
events.npc.rival.eden.04.choices.c.outco: Eden smiles. "That's more like you." You submit applications at the same desk on the same day. The clerk checks both names twice.
events.npc.rival.eden.05.title: The Last Night's Challenge
events.npc.rival.eden.05.body: Before the graduation observation, Eden waits atop the tower beside two telescopes. "A challenge. First to find a new star wins." Then adds, "Whoever finds it first, let's put both our names on the record."
events.npc.rival.eden.05.choices.a.label: "All right. I intend to win"
events.npc.rival.eden.05.choices.a.outco: At four in the morning, your telescope finds it first. Eden studies it, then writes both names. "A promise is a promise." Very quietly comes, "Congratulations."
Eden finds it first. You write both names as promised. Seeing this, Eden writes both on their own sheet too. "We saw it together anyway."
events.npc.rival.eden.05.choices.b.label: "No contest. Let's just look together"
events.npc.rival.eden.05.choices.b.outco: Both telescopes face the same way all night. You find nothing new, but write the same sentence on the last line of your separate sheets. Comparing them later makes you both laugh.
events.npc.rival.eden.05.choices.c.label: "I need sleep tonight"
events.npc.rival.eden.05.choices.c.outco: Eden does not stop you. "Right. Tomorrow's the real test." Looking back from the stairs, you see both telescopes still side by side. Eden is using only one.
events.npc.rival.eden.rivalry.title: Erasing a Name
events.npc.rival.eden.rivalry.body: Eden removes their name from your shared observation record. Arms folded, they say, "If it's joint work, no one knows who did what. Separate names. That's fair."
From that day, your records sit beside each other but never mix. Neither cites the other. It becomes very clear who did what.
Eden stands for a long time before unfolding their arms. "Maybe you're right." The names stay separate, but you examine each other's records more carefully afterward.
"This isn't about right and wrong." Eden leaves. The names split. That evening, you stare at a record bearing only your name.
events.npc.sera.eden.title: One of Two
events.npc.sera.eden.body: Sera can write only one recommendation to the royal observation corps. There are two candidates. She asks you first. "If it were Eden rather than you, what would you say?"
events.npc.sera.eden.choices.a.label: "Eden is better"
Sera recommends Eden. For you, she writes something else: a personal letter of introduction under her own name. It carries greater weight.
events.npc.sera.eden.choices.b.label: "I want the recommendation"
Sera nods and writes it. "Saying you want it is a qualification too." Eden congratulates you after learning about it. You cannot tell if the words are sincere.
events.npc.sera.eden.choices.c.label: "Could you recommend us both?"
Sera rereads the rules, then visits the dean. That year, the academy sends two letters. There is no precedent.
The rule permits one. Sera ultimately recommends Eden. Eden hears only that you asked for both of you. They never mention it.
events.npc.yun.01.title: A Road Off the Map
events.npc.yun.01.body: Yun unfolds an old map and points at an empty patch. "Here. No one's drawn it." The trip should take a day, at a time when every day matters.
events.npc.yun.01.choices.a.label: Go along
events.npc.yun.01.choices.a.outcomes.onl: The road is shorter than the map; the scenery lasts longer. On the way back, Yun adds a small mark to the blank.
events.npc.yun.01.choices.b.label: Borrow only the map
events.npc.yun.01.choices.b.outcomes.onl: You copy the map, thinking you will go someday. That someday may never come.
events.npc.yun.01.choices.c.label: Say you have work today
events.npc.yun.01.choices.c.outcomes.onl: Yun shrugs and leaves alone. Returning three days later, they say nothing.
events.npc.yun.02.title: Why Wander?
events.npc.yun.02.body: Outside the city gate, Yun lies on a hill with their pack for a pillow. "Best stars here. Better than the academy tower." A broad hat covers their face. "My name is written nowhere, so I can look from anywhere."
events.npc.yun.02.choices.a.label: "Does a name stop you seeing?"
events.npc.yun.02.choices.a.outcomes.onl: Yun lifts the hat. "Once you're written down, you see only what's written." The hat falls again. "You're only half written yet. A good time."
events.npc.yun.02.choices.b.label: Lie down and look together
events.npc.yun.02.choices.b.outcomes.onl: No one speaks for two hours. For the first time, you watch stars without naming a constellation. On the way down, Yun asks, "They don't teach that in class, do they?"
events.npc.yun.02.choices.c.label: "I want my name written down"
events.npc.yun.02.choices.c.outcomes.onl: Laughter comes from beneath the hat. "Then have it written well. I wander because I like seeing what named people become."
events.npc.yun.03.title: An Old Name
events.npc.yun.03.body: Yun sees the signature on a forty-year-old observation from the locked shelf. Their face stiffens. "That's my father." They remove the hat. "Expelled from the society for publishing something wrong. I don't think it was wrong."
events.npc.yun.03.choices.a.label: "Let's verify it together"
events.npc.yun.03.choices.a.outcomes.suc: The record is right. The instruments of forty years ago could not keep up. On the day you request a correction from the society, Yun enters the academy's main gate for the first time.
events.npc.yun.03.choices.a.outcomes.fai: Two weeks bring no conclusion. Yun folds the record. "It's all right. Two of us looked at something no one had checked." But Yun does not visit the hill that night.
events.npc.yun.03.choices.b.label: "Why haven't you tried yourself?"
events.npc.yun.03.choices.b.outcomes.onl: "No standing." Yun replaces the hat. "Only enrolled scholars can submit a verification." You have that standing. Yun did not show you the record to make you say so.
events.npc.yun.03.choices.c.label: Quietly close the record
events.npc.yun.03.choices.c.outcomes.onl: Yun thanks you sincerely. They leave the city before the season ends, then return in winter as though nothing happened.
events.npc.yun.04.title: Three Days Beyond the Border
events.npc.yun.04.body: Yun opens a map to a plateau three days away, beyond the academy's observation range. "Something appears only here. Once a year. This month." A finger crosses the border. "No permit. If we're caught, it'll go on your academic record."
events.npc.yun.04.choices.a.label: "Let's go"
events.npc.yun.04.choices.a.outcomes.suc: It rises on the third night. Your hands shake so much that you rewrite the record twice. On the return, Yun says, "Now you have something written nowhere too."
events.npc.yun.04.choices.a.outcomes.fai: The border post turns you back. A warning goes on your record. Yun apologizes. You have no regrets, though saying so takes three days.
events.npc.yun.04.choices.b.label: "Let's ask for permission"
events.npc.yun.04.choices.b.outcomes.onl: The dean delays for three days, then stamps approval. It becomes an official observation with Yun listed as companion. It is the first time Yun sees their own name on a document.
events.npc.yun.04.choices.c.label: "I can't go"
events.npc.yun.04.choices.c.outcomes.onl: Yun goes alone. Ten days later, they return with a copy. "Your share. Even if you didn't go." You stand a long time before accepting it.
events.npc.yun.05.title: Stay or Leave
events.npc.yun.05.body: Spring arrives. Yun's pack is ready. On the hill, they say, "The dean offered me a place. Guest observer." The hat rests on their knees longer than you have ever seen. "I don't know what being written down feels like."
events.npc.yun.05.choices.a.label: "Stay. You can see from here too"
events.npc.yun.05.choices.a.outcomes.suc: Yun unpacks. When their name is carved on the guest observer's plaque, they stand before it for a long time, hat in hand. The surname is their father's.
events.npc.yun.05.choices.a.outcomes.fai: Yun smiles and shakes their head. "I can leave because you said that." They depart that spring. Each season, unsigned observations reach the academy.
events.npc.yun.05.choices.b.label: "Go. But send your records"
events.npc.yun.05.choices.b.outcomes.onl: Yun replaces the hat. "I can do that." Afterward, one volume of observations belonging to no school arrives in the academy archive each season.
events.npc.yun.05.choices.c.label: "Could I come with you?"
events.npc.yun.05.choices.c.outcomes.onl: Yun waits a long time. "You're someone who needs a name." They fold an old map in half and give it to you. "Come after graduation. I'll keep the other half."
events.open.first-lesson.title: The First Lesson
events.open.first-lesson.body: Sera draws nine dots on the board. "This is you. How many will connect in twelve months is up to you." She sets down the chalk and surveys the room. "Why did you come?"
events.open.first-lesson.choices.a.label: "I came to read the stars"
events.open.first-lesson.choices.a.outco: "You say read." Sera writes something on the roll. "Seeing and reading are different. It usually takes half a year to understand how."
events.open.first-lesson.choices.b.label: "I came to make a living"
events.open.first-lesson.choices.b.outco: The classroom falls silent. Only Sera's expression stays the same. "Honest. That lasts longest." A student with glasses smiles silently in the back.
events.open.first-lesson.choices.c.label: "I don't know yet"
events.open.first-lesson.choices.c.outco: Sera picks up the chalk. "Then you've come to find out. That's a reason too." She draws a question mark beneath the nine dots.
events.open.gate.title: At the Main Gate
events.open.gate.body: At Starlight Academy's gate, the keeper finds and marks your name on the roll. "Twelve months. When winter comes twice, you leave." A bell rings inside. Everything you own is on your back.
events.open.gate.choices.a.label: Write your name carefully on the roll
events.open.gate.choices.a.outcomes.only: Keeping the letters inside the box takes time. The gatekeeper notices. "The ones who last tend to write that way."
events.open.gate.choices.b.label: Look up at the sky first
events.open.gate.choices.b.outcomes.only: Though it is daytime, one faint light remains in the west. The gatekeeper follows your gaze and smiles. "Not a star. Venus. First lesson will teach you that."
events.open.gate.choices.c.label: "Are twelve months enough?"
events.open.gate.choices.c.outcomes.only: Instead of answering, the gatekeeper closes the roll. "Enough for some, not for others." The gate opens. "The ones who ask were usually the former."
events.open.room.title: The Apprentice's Room
events.open.room.body: The last room on the third floor: one desk, one bed, one west-facing window. The previous occupant left a half-carved constellation on the sill. Setting down your bags suddenly makes the room seem smaller.
events.open.room.choices.a.label: Finish the constellation carving
events.open.room.choices.a.outcomes.only: Finding which constellation takes one hour; finishing it takes two. The finished carving lines up exactly with its place in the sky outside.
events.open.room.choices.b.label: Organize the desk first
events.open.room.choices.b.outcomes.only: A note waits inside the drawer. "The 3rd floor is cold in winter. Stuff paper into the window gaps." You follow the advice. It really is less cold.
events.open.room.choices.c.label: Just lie down
events.open.room.choices.c.outcomes.only: Looking at the ceiling, you hear an abacus from downstairs. You fall asleep to it and wake with a stiff neck.
events.opp.borrowed-robe.title: Borrowed Formalwear
events.opp.borrowed-robe.body: The dean's dinner is three days away. You have no formal robe. A fellow apprentice offers a loan. Even a cheap one would cost two months of food. You could simply stay home. The invitation lies on your desk.
events.opp.borrowed-robe.choices.a.label: Borrow from your classmate
events.opp.borrowed-robe.choices.a.outco: The sleeves are slightly long. You step on them twice, then roll them up. An elderly guest laughs and says the same thing happened to her first time.
events.opp.borrowed-robe.choices.b.label: Buy formalwear
events.opp.borrowed-robe.choices.b.outco: Properly fitted clothes straighten your posture. The dean asks your name, and everyone there hears it.
events.opp.borrowed-robe.choices.c.label: Do not go
events.opp.borrowed-robe.choices.c.outco: You observe from your room that night. The sky is clearer than the dinner hall, and you gain a page of notes. The invitation goes into a drawer.
events.opp.broken-lens.title: A Cracked Lens
events.opp.broken-lens.body: A hairline crack runs through the tower telescope's eyepiece. Replacing it is expensive. Leaving it would blur every observation this month. Perhaps Old Gu could polish it.
events.opp.broken-lens.choices.a.label: Try polishing it yourself
events.opp.broken-lens.choices.a.outcome: Three hours on the whetstone. Through the refitted lens, the stars are clearer than before. Your fingertips still tremble.
The crack spreads. Gu silently takes the lens. "Less force next time."
events.opp.broken-lens.choices.b.label: Pay to have it repaired
events.opp.broken-lens.choices.b.outcome: Two days later, it returns like new. The price hurts, but your observations are safe.
events.opp.broken-lens.choices.c.label: Observe through the blur
events.opp.broken-lens.choices.c.outcome: You compensate for the blurred image by eye. The notes are imperfect, but you learn more about seeing.
events.opp.clock-tower.title: The Stopped Clock Tower
events.opp.clock-tower.body: The square's clock has stopped for three days. The repairer says a part is missing and gives up. Without the bells, people struggle to measure the day. The tower door is unlocked.
events.opp.clock-tower.choices.a.label: Climb up and inspect the mechanism
events.opp.clock-tower.choices.a.outcome: The problem is a bird's nest caught in a shaft, not a missing part. You remove it gently. The second hand moves. Everyone in the square looks up at the bell.
You disturb a gear. The repairer comes up, restores it, and sighs. "Draw it before you touch it, I said."
events.opp.clock-tower.choices.b.label: Draw the mechanism
events.opp.clock-tower.choices.b.outcome: You spend three hours drawing the gears. With your diagram, the repairer fixes the clock in two days. The drawing hangs in city hall.
events.opp.clock-tower.choices.c.label: Walk past
events.opp.clock-tower.choices.c.outcome: The bell rings again the next day. No one knows who fixed it. You do not ask.
events.opp.coin-found.title: A Purse in the Road
events.opp.coin-found.body: A heavy leather purse lies at an alley corner. No one is nearby. There is no name inside.
events.opp.coin-found.choices.a.label: Leave it at the guard post
events.opp.coin-found.choices.a.outcomes: Three days later, the owner finds you and leaves a reward. It is less than the purse held, but your heart is light.
events.opp.coin-found.choices.b.label: Find the owner yourself
events.opp.coin-found.choices.b.outcomes: Two hours of asking around the market lead to a stallholder. From that day, you receive a greeting whenever you pass.
No one recognizes it. You leave it at the guard post and head home.
events.opp.coin-found.choices.c.label: Keep it
events.opp.coin-found.choices.c.outcomes: The purse feels heavier than expected. For several days, you take another route around the alley.
events.opp.commission-portrait.title: A Constellation Portrait
events.opp.commission-portrait.body: A woman asks a favor. "Paint the sky from the night my daughter was born. I'd like it on the wall." A date and time are enough for the calculation. The painting is another matter. She offers to pay in advance.
events.opp.commission-portrait.choices.a: Finding the stars takes one day; painting takes four. The woman stares in silence. Over the next four months, six similar commissions arrive.
The calculation is right, but the painting is not. She leaves the full payment. You try returning half, but she refuses.
events.opp.commission-portrait.choices.b: Calculate the sky and recommend an artist
You give the layout to a portrait painter in the square. The result is far better than yours would have been. The painter asks to work together again.
events.opp.commission-portrait.choices.c: She leaves politely, without showing disappointment. After closing the door, you briefly calculate that night's sky. It was a fine night.
events.opp.duel-request.title: A Challenge to Duel
events.opp.duel-request.body: An apprentice from another school calls your name in the square. "They say Starlight Academy copied our observations." It is false. A crowd gathers. Your challenger will not back down.
events.opp.duel-request.choices.a.label: Propose an observation contest
events.opp.duel-request.choices.a.outcom: That night, you measure the same star and compare notes. The smaller error wins. Your challenger apologizes publicly as promised, then offers a handshake.
Your error is larger. Your challenger asks for no apology. "I withdraw the copying claim." That hurts more.
events.opp.duel-request.choices.b.label: Demand evidence
events.opp.duel-request.choices.b.outcom: Three questions receive no answer. The crowd drifts away until only your challenger remains. The claim is never heard again.
Your challenger names a source. The name belongs to someone at your academy. You have no answer.
events.opp.duel-request.choices.c.label: Turn away
events.opp.duel-request.choices.c.outcom: Jeers follow your back, then fade beyond the square. Few remember the incident the next day.
events.opp.funeral-song.title: A Funeral Song
events.opp.funeral-song.body: The academy gatekeeper has died. With no family, the academy arranges the funeral. Everyone stands speechless before the coffin. In this city, a song is the customary farewell.
events.opp.funeral-song.choices.a.label: Step forward and sing
events.opp.funeral-song.choices.a.outcom: Your pitch is imperfect, but you finish. When the song ends, no one moves. Several people learn your name that day.
Your throat closes after two lines. Someone beside you continues. Soon several voices join. In the end, the song is finished.
events.opp.funeral-song.choices.b.label: Fetch an instrument and accompany them
events.opp.funeral-song.choices.b.outcom: You run to your room and back. With accompaniment, three people find the courage to sing. You keep your head down and your fingers on the strings until the end.
events.opp.funeral-song.choices.c.label: Stand quietly in place
events.opp.funeral-song.choices.c.outcom: No one sings. The square stays silent as the coffin leaves. Later, someone says that silence was a kind of courtesy too.
events.opp.hungry-winter.title: Winter Rations
events.opp.hungry-winter.body: After a bad harvest, the academy distributes rations. The line is long; apprentices receive one meal a day. You notice a child joining the line a second time. The server has not seen.
events.opp.hungry-winter.choices.a.label: Give the child your share
events.opp.hungry-winter.choices.a.outco: You miss dinner. The next day, the child recognizes you in the square and runs over with an apple from some unknown place.
events.opp.hungry-winter.choices.b.label: Explain to the server
events.opp.hungry-winter.choices.b.outco: After a moment's thought, the server makes a separate allowance for children. That line stays all winter. You pass it each time.
Rules are rules, comes the answer. The child never appears in line again. No one knows where they went.
events.opp.hungry-winter.choices.c.label: Pretend not to notice
events.opp.hungry-winter.choices.c.outco: Three days later, the server catches the child and sends them away. You see it happen without putting down your chopsticks.
events.opp.lantern-order.title: One Hundred Lanterns
events.opp.lantern-order.body: The festival committee urgently needs someone to paint constellations on one hundred lanterns in three days. The original painter injured a hand. "Knowing the stars matters more than painting well."
events.opp.lantern-order.choices.a.label: Work alone for three days
events.opp.lantern-order.choices.a.outco: You finish all one hundred. On festival night, the lanterns match the real night sky. Few notice, but those who do stand for a long time.
Your hand stiffens after eighty. The committee fills in the rest at random. You receive eight-tenths of the pay. One corner of the square belongs to no real sky.
events.opp.lantern-order.choices.b.label: Gather people and divide the work
events.opp.lantern-order.choices.b.outco: Six people finish in two days. You draw the layouts and inspect the work. On festival night, each stands like a portrait beneath their own lanterns.
Everyone knows a different version of each constellation. Corrections take longer than painting. You redraw half the lanterns yourself.
events.opp.lantern-order.choices.c.label: Decline the job
events.opp.lantern-order.choices.c.outco: On festival night, the lanterns bear flower patterns. They are pretty enough.
events.opp.lost-child.title: A Child in the Square
events.opp.lost-child.body: A child cries in the square. Adults walk past. The child can say nothing beyond their name. The sun is sinking.
events.opp.lost-child.choices.a.label: Help find the child's home
events.opp.lost-child.choices.a.outcomes: Three alleys lead you to the right door. The child's mother holds both your hands for a long time.
You search until night, then leave the child at the guard post. The next day, you hear only that the child reached home.
events.opp.lost-child.choices.b.label: Take the child to the guard post
events.opp.lost-child.choices.b.outcomes: A guard takes the child in their arms. It is the right thing, and leaves you a little sad.
events.opp.lost-child.choices.c.label: Walk past
events.opp.lost-child.choices.c.outcomes: You do not look back. Sleep comes late that night.
